Airain.name: Type 20
Airain.desc: A faithful remake of the 1950s French air force pilot's chronograph, with a flyback button that resets and restarts the timer in one press.

Airain.name: Type 21
Airain.desc: The Type 20's sibling with a glossy black dial, based on a vintage piece sold at Sotheby's.

Airain.name: Sous-Marine Re-Edition
Airain.desc: A compact 200m dive watch revived from Airain's 1960s archive, with details chosen by community vote.

Space One.name: Jumping Hour
Space One.movement: Automatic, Soprod base with in-house jumping-hour module
Space One.desc: A futuristic watch that shows the hour as a big number that jumps forward, with a sweeping arc for minutes.

Space One.name: Tellurium
Space One.movement: Automatic, Soprod P024 with in-house Earth and moon module
Space One.desc: Shows a tiny Earth and moon turning in real time, a rare astronomical display at this price.

Space One.name: Worldtimer
Space One.movement: Automatic, Soprod P024 with in-house world-time module
Space One.desc: A space-age world-time watch that shows the time in every major city at a glance.

Vulcain.name: Cricket
Vulcain.desc: The famous mechanical alarm watch worn by US presidents, which buzzes loudly at the time you set.

Vulcain.name: Skindiver
Vulcain.desc: A slim 1960s-style dive watch, now in Mark II form with 300m water resistance and a ceramic bezel.

Vulcain.name: Skindiver Chronograph
Vulcain.desc: A retro diving chronograph revived from the archives, rated to 200m.

Vulcain.name: Monopusher
Vulcain.desc: A vintage-style chronograph that starts, stops and resets with a single button in the crown.

Vulcain.name: Nautical
Vulcain.desc: A dive watch with a built-in alarm, originally meant to remind divers when to surface.

Aquastar.name: Deepstar
Aquastar.desc: A revived 1960s diving chronograph with a regatta-style countdown, made in small yearly batches.

Aquastar.name: Deepstar II
Aquastar.desc: A compact, colourful 200m dive watch based on Aquastar's 1960s designs.

Aquastar.name: Benthos
Aquastar.desc: Remakes of Aquastar's 1970s professional dive watch, from the affordable Heritage to the 500m Benthos 500 II.

Aquastar.name: Airstar
Aquastar.desc: A pilot's chronograph from 1965, linked to free-diver Jacques Mayol and Philippe Cousteau.

Amida.name: Digitrend
Amida.movement: Automatic, Soprod Newton P092 with jumping-hour module
Amida.desc: A 1970s driver's watch revived, reading the time from numbers on the side so you can check it while holding a wheel.

Amida.name: Digitrend Open Sapphire
Amida.movement: Automatic, Soprod Newton P092 with jumping-hour module
Amida.desc: A limited Digitrend with a see-through sapphire case that shows the moving parts inside.

Kollokium.name: Projekt 02
Kollokium.desc: A sculptural, bezel-less steel watch with a tall domed crystal, designed by a group of well-known watch designers.

Kollokium.name: Projekt 01
Kollokium.desc: The brand's first, cushion-shaped sports watch; the series has now ended, so buy from dealers or resale.

Straum.name: Jan Mayen
Straum.desc: A Norwegian integrated-bracelet sports watch with dials inspired by Arctic ice and northern lights.

Straum.name: Expedition
Straum.desc: A tougher outdoor tool watch spun off the Jan Mayen, with crown guards and a date.

Behrens.name: Rotary
Behrens.desc: An avant-garde watch whose time display rotates like a turntable, an early award-nominated design from this Chinese independent.

Behrens.name: The Dark Knight
Behrens.desc: A steel tourbillon, a spinning cage that evens out timekeeping, at a fraction of the usual Swiss price.

Behrens.name: Navigraph
Behrens.desc: One of Behrens' more affordable designs, with its trademark unconventional dial layout.

Behrens.name: Starship II
Behrens.desc: Behrens' entry-level model, offering its sci-fi styling at an accessible price.

Behrens.name: Ultralight
Behrens.desc: A titanium watch weighing about 20 grams, made to disappear on the wrist.

Celadon.name: Century
Celadon.desc: Celadon's high-end line with Chinese artisan dials in lacquer and cloisonne enamel, made to order.

Celadon.name: CL Imperial
Celadon.desc: A dressy Chinese-made watch with patterned dials inspired by imperial art.

Celadon.name: Imperial
Celadon.desc: The brand's original line with guilloche Plum Blossom and Peacock dials; reportedly being wound down.

anOrdain.name: Model 2
anOrdain.desc: A Scottish watch with a handmade vitreous enamel dial, made to order with a long waiting list.

anOrdain.name: Model 1
anOrdain.movement: Automatic, La Joux-Perret G101 / decorated A1
anOrdain.desc: A simple everyday watch, now offered with a porcelain dial that skips the enamel waiting list.

anOrdain.name: Model 3
anOrdain.desc: A slimmer sports-style model with enamel dials, including the wood-grain 'Method' edition.

Atelier Wen.name: Perception
Atelier Wen.desc: An integrated-bracelet steel sports watch with a hand-cut guilloche dial made in China; the V3 arrived in 2026.

Atelier Wen.name: Ancestra
Atelier Wen.desc: A new dress watch that brings Atelier Wen's handcrafted dials to a classic round case.

Atelier Wen.name: Perception Millesime
Atelier Wen.desc: Yearly limited Perception editions with special dials such as wood or pietersite stone.

Kurono Tokyo.name: Grand Jubilee Calendar
Kurono Tokyo.desc: A dressy triple-calendar watch showing day, date and month, designed by Japanese master Hajime Asaoka.

Kurono Tokyo.name: Jubilee Sensu
Kurono Tokyo.desc: A dress watch with a power-reserve gauge shaped like a Japanese folding fan.

Kurono Tokyo.name: Anniversary
Kurono Tokyo.desc: Hajime Asaoka's elegant, affordable dress watch, sold in short online windows; Mori and Toki are its colourways.

Kurono Tokyo.name: Chronograph
Kurono Tokyo.desc: A vintage-style chronograph with richly coloured dials, made in small batches.

Selten.name: Grand Feu Enamel Flare
Selten.desc: A Hong Kong-designed watch with a kiln-fired enamel dial over an engraved flare pattern, rare at this price.

Selten.name: Grand Feu Enamel Spiral
Selten.desc: The same glossy fired-enamel dial, this time over a spiral engraving.

Ophion.name: OPH 786
Ophion.desc: A Spanish dress watch inspired by Breguet, with hand-guilloche-style dials and a finely decorated movement.

Ophion.name: OPH 786 Velos
Ophion.desc: A teardrop-lug version designed with input from Kari Voutilainen's workshop.

Omega.name: Seamaster Diver 300M
Omega.desc: Omega's signature dive watch with a wave-pattern dial, famous as James Bond's watch.

Omega.name: Speedmaster Moonwatch Professional
Omega.desc: The chronograph NASA approved for spaceflight and worn on the Moon in 1969.

Omega.name: Seamaster Aqua Terra
Omega.desc: A smart, versatile everyday watch with a teak-pattern dial that works with a suit or jeans.

Omega.name: Constellation
Omega.desc: Omega's dressy line, known for the 'claws' that hold its bezel in place.

Omega.name: Seamaster Planet Ocean
Omega.desc: A heavier-duty 600m dive watch with a ceramic bezel.

Breitling.name: Navitimer
Breitling.desc: The classic pilot's chronograph with a slide-rule bezel for flight calculations.

Breitling.name: Superocean
Breitling.desc: A colourful 1950s-style dive watch, Breitling's most affordable mechanical line.

Breitling.name: Chronomat
Breitling.desc: Breitling's everyday sport watch with a rouleaux bracelet, relaunched with a cleaner design in 2026.

Breitling.name: Avenger
Breitling.desc: A rugged, oversized aviation tool watch, offered as three-hand, GMT and chronograph.

Breitling.name: Top Time
Breitling.desc: A colourful 1960s-inspired chronograph line with bright dials and limited editions.

Breitling.name: Premier
Breitling.desc: Breitling's dressier chronographs, inspired by its 1940s designs.
